podcast_name: Coffee & Cap Rates: Commercial Real Estate Podcast
episode_title: 131. Brooklyn Real Estate: Development, Distress & Opportunity in 2026 featuring Sean R. Kelly, Esq.
question: How did policy alignment and tax incentives drive a 60% year-over-year increase in development transaction volume in Brooklyn during the first half of 2026?
transcript_excerpt: The surge was driven by a combination of the 485 tax abatement program for projects under 99 units and the rezoning of the Atlantic Avenue corridor in Crown Heights and Bed-Stuy. Of the $1 billion in transactional volume, $300 million came from transactions in the greater downtown Brooklyn area, reflecting a flight to quality. Additionally, improved pricing across development sectors and increased land prices due to higher rents in supply-constrained markets contributed to the momentum.

question: What drove major office-to-residential conversion projects in Brooklyn's Navy Yard area post-COVID?
transcript_excerpt: A large transaction in the Navy Yard in Clinton Hill, originally slated as an office conversion five to six years ago, was rezoned post-COVID when the office market struggled significantly. This rezoning allowed the owners to sell the site and likely exit whole while enabling the creation of approximately 700 units in a supply-constrained market with a strong job hub nearby.

question: What is driving long-term family owners and generational landlords to exit the rent-stabilized housing market in New York City?
transcript_excerpt: Long-term owners, patient capital, and family offices—some of whom built buildings in Brooklyn generations ago—are exiting due to a combination of HSTPA regulations, increased operating costs, non-cooperating capital markets, and more recently, 0% rent increase orders. This is described as the first time in nearly 20 years of business that such an exodus of generational owners is occurring, representing a significant shift in the market.

question: What affordable housing and residential development activity has been recorded in Brooklyn's development sector year-to-date?
transcript_excerpt: In Brooklyn alone, $130 million in real estate development transactions have been completed this year covering affordable housing, condominiums, and townhouses. An additional $100 million in transactions were in contract, representing demand across all segments of the development market.

question: How are smaller free-market and tax-protected residential buildings performing in emerging Brooklyn neighborhoods in 2026?
transcript_excerpt: Smaller free-market and tax-protected buildings are trading well in up-and-coming locations in Brooklyn, contributing to continued activity in the second half of 2026. Market participants view purchasing well-maintained rent-stabilized housing stock in good locations managed by the same families for 20, 30, or 40 years as potentially one of the best investment bets in New York City.

question: What major portfolio sales in rent-stabilized Brooklyn residential property signaled market stress in 2025-2026?
transcript_excerpt: Major sell-offs included the Pinnacle portfolio sale with a significant Brooklyn portion, and Lethrax's sale of a $30+ million rent-stabilized portfolio. These transactions reflect broader stress in the rent-stabilized housing sector as long-term owners increasingly exit the market.
